Fast-Poly introduces a polyhedral framework to address 3D MOT challenges such as rotational anisotropy and computational inefficiency. The core innovation lies in replacing traditional bounding-box-based IoU/GIoU with polyhedral affinity metrics that better reflect spatial relationships under rotation. This is achieved through a combination of geometric filtering, voxel-based cost estimation, and parallelized processing pipelines. The system assumes that 3D objects can be approximated as polyhedra and that rotational effects can be captured via SO(3) transformations. Its breakdown regime occurs when object shapes deviate significantly from polyhedral models or when voxel resolution fails to resolve fine-grained spatial detail. Dualities emerge between geometric accuracy and computational efficiency, where increasing polyhedral fidelity improves tracking but also increases complexity. Failure modes include misalignment of polyhedral representations during rotation and over-reliance on coarse voxel grids in cluttered scenes.
